newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Stadium Australia sees A$200 mln float shortfall.
newsitem.headline: Stadium Australia sees A$200 mln float shortfall.

text.p: Stadium Australia Chairman Peter Ritchie on Wednesday confirmed that underwriters to the A$364.4 million float of 35,000 gold and platinum passes had only sold about 40 percent of the passes, leaving a float shortfall of over A$200 million.
Ritchie told ABC Radio only about 40 percent of the passes had been sold, but that underwriters were confident of selling the Olympic tickets that were part of the passes before the 2000 Olympics.
"I understand they've sold about 40 percent," Ritchie was quoted as saying by ABC.

"The underwriters are confident that they (the passes) will appreciate in value, certainly the olympic seats aspects will appreciate between now and the games as the games get closer and as people realise they are all prime seats," Ritchie told ABC radio.

A Stadium Australia spokeswoman said the underwriters, ANZ Securities, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Macquarie Bank Ltd and ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, are not due to announce the exact results of the float until Friday.
The Stadium Australia float, which closed last Thursday, has been open for almost six months, more than twice as long as most share offers.
Its offer of 34,400 gold packages at A$10,000 each and 600 platinum passes at A$33,000 each opened on October 7 and its closing date has been extended twice due to lack of demand.

The gold packages included a seat at every stadium session of the 2000 Olympic Games, stadium membership for 30 years and 1,000 shares in the stadium company itself. The platinum package includes two priority seats and membership privileges.
